title: A Parish for the Alibi
premise: Edmund Zhou, host of the true-crime podcast 'The Alibi Parish,' has quietly solved three deaths ruled accidental, and her anonymous reputation precedes her when a nervous client, Marlowe Voss, pays a year's retainer to prove that his wealthy uncle, Aldous Voss, will NOT be murdered — though no body exists yet. Digging into the Voss estate, Edmund discovers an inheritance ledger disguised as parish tithing records at St. Anselm's, mapping who inherits what upon each family member's death, with the final entry dated eleven days out: Aldous himself. As she decodes the ledger, she falls for Marlowe even as evidence tightens around him as the likely heir-killer, forcing her to choose between duty to her client's secret and justice for a man still breathing. In the climax, Edmund stages a fake death using the ledger's own logic to flush out the true architect — Aldous's nurse and illegitimate daughter, Ruth — who has been manipulating Marlowe's grief and debts all along; Aldous lives, the ledger becomes evidence, and Edmund chooses love over the anonymity her work depends on.
about_author: Xanthe Quintana is a former probate clerk who spent seven years reading other people's last wishes before turning them into fiction. She writes from a converted vestry on the coast of Maine, where she keeps a shelf of unsolved case files she promises never to podcast about.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A cold open recaps how Edmund quietly solved three 'accidental' deaths through her podcast, establishing her methods and her rule: never meet clients. The chapter ends with a retainer arriving in cash, postmarked from her own town, asking her to prevent a murder that hasn't happened yet. Beat: intrigue laced with unease.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wants Nothing Found
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Against her rule, Edmund meets Marlowe Voss in a shuttered boathouse; he is charming, evasive, and terrified of something he won't name. He insists his uncle Aldous will die within weeks and wants it proven premeditated — by someone. Edmund takes the case against instinct. Beat: attraction shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: St. Anselm's Tithes
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Following the Voss family's generations-long tie to St. Anselm's parish, Edmund photographs centuries of tithing ledgers and notices columns that don't balance — names paired with sums matching modern property values. Beat: the thrill of the first real clue.

chapters.title: A House That Counts Its Dead
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund tours Voss Hall under a pretext, cataloguing portraits whose dates of death align eerily with the ledger's entries. The housekeeper, Mrs. Pell, warns her off with a line that chills: 'This family settles its accounts.' Beat: dread settling in like weather.

chapters.title: Ruth, Who Never Leaves the Room
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund interviews Aldous's live-in nurse, Ruth Calloway, gentle and watchful, who answers every question with another question. Aldous himself, sharp-tongued and lucid, tells Edmund he expects to die soon and finds it funny. Beat: two suspects introduced, both disarming.

chapters.title: Marlowe's Debts
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Financial digging reveals Marlowe is drowning — gambling debts, a mortgaged flat — and stands to inherit everything if Aldous dies before a contested codicil takes effect. The evidence points exactly where Marlowe doesn't want it to. Beat: betrayal blooming in Edmund's chest.

chapters.title: The Ledger Decoded
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Working nights in the parish archive, Edmund cracks the cipher: the ledger is a death-order map of the inheritance, updated in fresh ink, with the final entry — Aldous Voss — dated eleven days hence. Someone is still writing in it. Beat: triumph curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: What the Podcast Cannot Say
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund's producer, Devi, pushes back as Edmund goes dark, refusing to air anything on the Voss case. Flashback threads reveal why Edmund works anonymously: a past case destroyed an innocent man. Beat: vulnerability exposed; stakes become personal.

chapters.title: An Accident, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund discovers the stairwell at Voss Hall has been subtly altered — a loosened banister bracket, waxed treads — mirroring the method from one of her three solved cases. The killer knows her work. Beat: hunter realizing she is also hunted.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund confronts Marlowe with the evidence; he breaks down and admits he knew about the ledger but swears he was being coached — anonymous letters promising debt relief if he simply stayed silent. Beat: pity warring with doubt; the romance deepens in confession.

chapters.title: Mrs. Pell's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The housekeeper reveals the family's buried secret: Aldous had a daughter born out of wedlock decades ago, written out of every will — and the ledger's oldest entries are in a woman's hand. Beat: the mystery pivots from greed to grievance.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. With nine days left, Edmund requests police help and is rebuffed — no crime, no victim, no standing. She realizes justice must be built outside the law or not at all. Beat: isolation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Second Codicil
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund locates a hidden second codicil restoring the lost daughter's inheritance, signed but undated — meaning whoever controls the date controls everything. The ledger isn't predicting deaths; it's scheduling them. Beat: the full horror of the design lands.

chapters.title: Someone Follows Her Home
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund's flat is searched; her case files photographed; a page of the ledger left on her pillow like a calling card. Marlowe insists on staying to protect her, and duty and desire finally collide. Beat: fear and tenderness braided together.

chapters.title: Aldous Tells the Truth, Mostly
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Aldous confesses he wrote the codicil after learning of his daughter, but refuses to name her, saying he intends to let 'the account settle itself.' Edmund realizes he may be courting death as penance. Beat: moral vertigo — the victim complicit in the plot.

chapters.title: The Handwriting
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Graphological comparison confirms the recent ledger entries match nursing charts signed R. Calloway — but Ruth produces an alibi so airtight it feels manufactured. Edmund begins suspecting the alibi itself is the performance. Beat: certainty dissolving.

chapters.title: Seven Days, One Plan
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Out of legal options, Edmund devises a gambit: fake Aldous's death on schedule, publish the obituary, and let the ledger's author come to collect. Marlowe agrees to play grieving heir. Beat: resolve sharpened into risk; love declared in the planning.

chapters.title: The Death of Aldous Voss
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The staged death unfolds — a hired doctor, a sealed room, a weeping household — and Edmund watches Ruth's face for the tell. It comes: not grief, but arithmetic. Beat: high tension, the trap sprung, hearts pounding.

chapters.title: The Account Settled
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Confronted with the dated codicil and the ledger, Ruth confesses: she is the daughter, and the letters coaching Marlowe were hers — a test to see if any Voss deserved saving. Aldous, alive, hears everything. Beat: catharsis and heartbreak entwined.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The family must choose: prosecution or private settlement. Aldous signs the codicil, restores Ruth's name, and asks only that the ledger stay out of court. Edmund records nothing — her hardest professional act. Beat: mercy weighed against principle.

chapters.title: The Episode That Never Airs
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund burns the case from her files and records a decoy episode instead, protecting everyone including herself. Devi senses the sacrifice; the podcast's mystique grows on a story Edmund can never tell. Beat: quiet grief for the truth unlived publicly.

chapters.title: A Parish for the Alibi
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Weeks later, Edmund and Marlowe walk the St. Anselm's grounds where the ledger began; Ruth tends the archive openly now. Edmund chooses to keep meeting clients, keep risking, keep loving — the alibi no longer needed. Beat: resolution warm, open-eyed, earned.
